name: Mishmannah
overview: Mishmannah was a male member of the tribe of Gad, noted in Scripture as the fourth Gadite to join David. He came to David at Ziklag, marking his allegiance during a critical period of David's rise. His role is briefly recorded, highlighting his participation among Gadite warriors who supported David.
namesAndTitles: The name Mishmannah means 'fatness' in Hebrew. It is a proper name mentioned in 1 Chronicles 12:10 without indication that it was given directly by God. The name itself does not carry additional titles or divine attribution.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Mishmannah was a descendant of Gad, one of the twelve tribes of Israel. Beyond this tribal affiliation, no other family relationships are documented for him.
scriptureSignificance: Mishmannah's significance lies in his early support of David, as he was among those from the tribe of Gad who came to join David at Ziklag. Being the fourth Gadite to do so, he represents the loyalty and military backing David received from the tribe of Gad during a formative time in his leadership. His mention underscores the broad coalition of Israelite tribes recognizing David's future kingship.
